original_value: We consider the System Optimal Dynamic Traffic Assignment (SO-DTA) problem with Partial Control for general networks with physical queuing. Our goal is to optimally control any subset of the networks agents to minimize the total congestion of all agents in the network. We adopt a flow dynamics model that is a Godunov discretization of the Lighthill–Williams–Richards partial differential equation with a triangular flux function and a corresponding multicommodity junction solver. The partial control formulation generalizes the SO-DTA problem to consider cases where only a fraction of the total flow can be controlled, as may arise in the context of certain incentive schemes. This leads to a nonconvex multicommodity optimization problem. We define a multicommodity junction model that only requires full Lagrangian paths for the controllable agents, and aggregate turn ratios for the noncontrollable (selfish) agents. We show how the resulting finite horizon nonlinear optimal control problem can be efficiently solved using the discrete adjoint method, leading to gradient computations that are linear in the size of the state space and the controls.  The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2017.0800 .

result.paraphrase: We study the System Optimal Dynamic Traffic Assignment (SO-DTA) problem with partial control on general networks with physical queuing. The objective is to optimally regulate any chosen subset of agents in the network so as to minimize overall congestion for all agents. We use a flow dynamics model based on a Godunov discretization of the Lighthill–Williams–Richards partial differential equation, with a triangular flux function and an associated multicommodity junction solver. This partial-control setting extends the SO-DTA problem to situations in which only part of the total flow is controllable, as can happen under certain incentive schemes, yielding a nonconvex multicommodity optimization problem. We formulate a multicommodity junction model that needs complete Lagrangian paths only for controllable agents, while using aggregate turn ratios for noncontrollable (selfish) agents. We demonstrate that the resulting finite-horizon nonlinear optimal control problem can be solved efficiently with the discrete adjoint method, producing gradient calculations that scale linearly with the sizes of the state space and the controls. The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2017.0800 .
